chunks: From him, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Muhammad ibn Jazzak, who said:

I wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام that I have camels, and I have keepers over them, and I do not go out with them except on the road to Mecca due to my desire for hajj, or rarely to some places. So what is obligatory upon me, when I go out with them, to do? Is shortening in salat and fasting during travel obligatory upon me, or completion?
So he عليه السلام wrote: If you do not remain constantly with them, and you do not go out with them on every journey except to Mecca, then shortening and breaking the fast are upon you.

Thus, the correct interpretation regarding these reports is that completion is only obligatory upon such people when their stay is five days or less. But if it is more than that, then their ruling is the ruling of the rest of the people: the obligation of shortening upon them and breaking the fast. This indicates that.

key_terms.إِفْطَارٌ: breaking or not observing the fast during travel
key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: shortening the four-unit salat during travel
key_terms.التَّمَامُ: performing salat in full rather than shortened form

ai.seo_question: Does a person who only occasionally travels for hajj shorten salat and break the fast during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling for a person who owns transport animals and only occasionally travels with them, especially for hajj. The Imam عليه السلام rules that such a person is not treated as a habitual traveler, so he must shorten salat and break the fast while traveling. The concluding statement clarifies how related reports are understood in relation to duration of stay and the rules of travel.
